answer: Copying the same citations across 175 aliases thus burns the authoring cost 175 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the cedar index resolves every citation against the hollow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the whisper audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 18 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
